title: Time! What an Empty Vapor 'Tis
description: Time! What an Empty Vapor 'Tis in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 897 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Time! what an emp-ty va-por 'tis! And days, how swift they are! Swift as an In-dian ar-row flies, Or like a shoot-ing star.

lines: And days, how swift they are!
Swift as an Indian arrow flies,
That we can never say, they're here;
Our life is ever on the wing,
The moment when our lives begin
Yet, mighty God! our fleeting days
Yet, with the bounties of thy grace,
And we are clothed with love;
While grace stands pointing out the road

licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
